questions.text:
A given program has 25% load/store instructions. Suppose the ideal CPI (cycles per
instruction) without any memory stalls is 2. The program exhibits 2% miss rate on
instruction cache and 8% miss rate on data cache. The miss penalty is 100 cycles.
The speedup (rounded off to two decimal places) achieved with a perfect cache (i.e.,
with NO data or instruction cache misses) is _________
questions.solution:
Every instruction is fetched (I-cache) and 25% also access data (D-cache).

Stall cycles per instruction:
- I-cache: [latex]1\times0.02\times100=2[/latex]
- D-cache: [latex]0.25\times0.08\times100=2[/latex]

Actual CPI [latex]=2+2+2=6[/latex], perfect-cache CPI [latex]=2[/latex].

Speedup [latex]=6/2=3.00[/latex]

Answer: 3

Click here for detail solution by gateoverflow

In each iteration every existing process calls fork(), so the number of processes doubles, and each of them prints once. (wait() only changes the order, not the count; each child continues the loop with the current x.)

- x = 3: 1 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 2 processes, prints 2
- x = 2: 2 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 4 processes, prints 4
- x = 1: 4 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 8 processes, prints 8

Total [latex]=2+4+8=14[/latex]

Answer: 14

questions.text:
Consider the entries shown below in the forwarding table of an [latex] \mathbb{P} [/latex] router. Each entry consists of an IP prefix and the corresponding next hop router for packets whose destination IP address matches the prefix. The notation "[latex] \mathrm{/N} [/latex]" in a prefix indicates a subnet mask with the most significant [latex] \mathrm{N} [/latex] bits set to 1.

[latex] \begin{array}{|l|c|} \hline Prefix & Next\; hop \; router \\ \hline 10.1 .1 .0 / 24 & R1 \\ \hline 10.1 .1 .128 / 25 & R2 \\ \hline 10.1 .1 .64 / 26 & R3 \\ \hline 10.1 .1 .192 / 26 & R4 \\ \hline \end{array}[/latex]

This router forwards 20 packets each to 5 hosts. The IP addresses of the hosts are 10.1.1.16, 10.1.1.72, 10.1.1.132, 10.1.1.191, and 10.1.1.205. The number of packets forwarded via the next hop router [latex] R 2 [/latex] is
questions.solution:
Use longest prefix match. Address ranges (last byte):
/24 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 0-255 (R1), .128/25 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 128-255 (R2), .64/26 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 64-127 (R3), .192/26 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 192-255 (R4).

- 10.1.1.16 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] only /24 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] R1
- 10.1.1.72 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] /26 (64-127) [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] R3
- 10.1.1.132 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] /25 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] R2
- 10.1.1.191 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] /25 (not in 192-255) [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] R2
- 10.1.1.205 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] /26 (192-255) [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] R4

R2 gets 2 hosts [latex]\times[/latex] 20 packets [latex]=40[/latex].

Answer: 40

questions.text: Let [latex] G=(V, \Sigma, S, P) [/latex] be a context-free grammar in Chomsky Normal Form with [latex] \Sigma=\{a, b, c\} [/latex] and [latex] V [/latex] containing 10 variable symbols including the start symbol [latex] S [/latex]. The string [latex] w=a^{30} b^{30} c^{30} [/latex] is derivable from [latex] S [/latex]. The number of steps (application of rules) in the derivation [latex] S \rightarrow^* w [/latex] is _____
questions.solution:
CNF rules are [latex]A\rightarrow BC[/latex] or [latex]A\rightarrow a[/latex].

- Each [latex]A\rightarrow BC[/latex] increases the number of symbols by 1. To grow from 1 symbol (S) to [latex]n[/latex] symbols needs [latex]n-1[/latex] such steps.
- Each of the [latex]n[/latex] variables is then turned into a terminal by [latex]A\rightarrow a[/latex]: [latex]n[/latex] steps.

Total [latex]=2n-1[/latex]. Here [latex]n=|w|=90[/latex]: [latex]2(90)-1=179[/latex].

Answer: 179

questions.text: The number of edges present in the forest generated by the DFS traversal of an undirected graph [latex] G [/latex] with 100 vertices is 40 . The number of connected components in [latex] G [/latex] is ____
questions.solution:
DFS produces one tree per connected component. A tree with [latex]k[/latex] vertices has [latex]k-1[/latex] edges, so a forest with [latex]n[/latex] vertices and [latex]c[/latex] trees has [latex]n-c[/latex] edges.

[latex]100-c=40\Rightarrow c=60[/latex]

Answer: 60
